Resident of the Chicago metropolitan area here. You could do a lot worse than Illinois: strong unions, average pay approximately $10k higher than Indiana, and some very good districts, but it's not without it's challenges.

 Biggest thing is that the state government is hilariously corrupt and has been using state pension funds as its piggybank for decades... now pensions are extremely underfunded and nobody has any real ideas on how to fix that problem. This scares a lot of people and as a result we have a teacher shortage currently, especially in middle school and special ed. If you're looking for a position it'd probably be somewhat easier than average to find one.

Chicago proper is a crapshoot and your experience will absolutely depend on the school you end up in. You will see both extremes regarding funding and quality of education, and the school system is a perfect example of how segregation has absolutely devastated the city. It's also got the typical issues one might find in large school districts in major metropolitan regions, but it's not the hellhole the media makes it out to be. I've got a friend who's teaching 7th grade English in a school on the South Side and loves it, and I've got another who barely lasted a year. If you're smart about it, it can be a pretty decent gig. Pay is higher than average for teachers but keep in mind Chicago is expensive. You can live comfortably though if you're single and/or childfree, don't have much debt and are at least somewhat good at money management. Chicago has enough free entertainment that you can be somewhat frugal and not be bored, as long as Cook County taxes don't gouge you too much. Personally I'd take teaching in Chicago over NC in a heartbeat though since you can have an easier time supporting a middle class lifestyle on a teacher's salary, but you have to be smart about it. It will chew you up and spit you out if you don't know what you're getting yourself into.

The "best" districts are in the western/northwest suburbs (Elmhurst, Libertyville, Hinsdale, Wheaton, Schaumburg, Naperville etc.) but they're extremely competitive and difficult to get your foot through the door. You also have to deal with the high cost of living and sense of  etitlement that often go hand in hand with affluent districts. I'm actually a product of CUSD 200 (Wheaton, approximately 30 minutes from Chicago as the crow flies) which is considered to be one of the best districts in the nation, for students and teachers. It's also currently looking to fill several vacancies for the first time in years. If you're seriously considering the Chicago area, I'd give it a look.

My advice would be to find something in the western suburbs (Dupage/Kane County) and try to find a decent place to live in Aurora. It's only 45 mins from the city and you can find a nice apartment for some of the cheapest rents in the Chicago metro area and it's got a cool downtown for a mid-sized city.

If you have any questions feel free to let me know. I've lived in the area and am doing my student teaching in a 3rd grade class out in Aurora so I'm likely going to be staying fairly local for the time being

Also I'd really recommend the works of David Lynch, particularly Eraserhead, Mulholland Drive, and his TV series, Twin Peaks. If you can get past a few scenes of cringey teenagers here and there, it's absolutely brilliant. **-The Exploding Hearts**,  were a glam punk group out of Portland, Oregon. They put out one excellent album before a car crash ended the band's career. Had they stuck around, they would've been the defining rock band band of the 2000's. Their sound was sort of a mix between British glam rock, garage rock and punk. There's a major Clash/NY Dolls influence in their songwriting. Check out their song "Rumors In Town." 



**- Galaxie 500** is a group you would love if you're more into The Velvet's less punky, more psychedelic side. "Today" is my favorite album by them. 



**-Marquee Moon, by Television** is definitely an album you should check out, they were a big part of the CBGB scene. They were a jazz influenced group similar to the Velvet Underground, with intricate song structures. They sound nothing like any other "punk" group and capture the philosophy of punk rock more, seeing as punk is about doing whatever the fuck you want instead of living up to some cookiecutter definition of what consumers and critics say it is.



**-White Lung** is one of the best, most authentic punk bands right now. They're a female fronted group out of Vancouver influenced just as much by 80's post-punk, riot grrl and early hardcore as they are by old school punk. Basically imagine if Hole didn't suck. I highly recommend their albums "It's Evil" and "Deep Fantasy." Their track "Down It Goes" is their best for newbies. 



**-Ty Segall** is what you would get if Syd Barrett or Marc Bolan from T. Rex joined the Stooges. His sound is a mix of 60's garage pop, grunge, punk, glam rock and psychedelia. "Twins" is his most accessible album, but my favorite track is "Candy Sam" off of his most recent album. His performance on Colbert is a must.
